Core mental model
Daily = noisy day-to-day signal · MA7 = short-term regime · MA30 = structural baseline · Percentile = historical placement
This same mental model is used on landing tiles, chain dashboards, and in methodology.
Global definitions

Concepts

One mental model (Daily / MA7 / MA30 / Percentile)
Basic
  • Daily = the actual day’s activity (noisy).
  • MA7 = short-term regime (last-week baseline).
  • MA30 = structural baseline (last-month baseline).
  • Percentile = where today ranks versus historical values in the chosen window.
Advanced
MA_n(t) = (1/n) · Σ_{i=0..n-1} x_{t-i}
Δ(daily vs MA7) = (x_t − MA7_t) / |MA7_t|
Δ(MA7 vs MA30) = (MA7_t − MA30_t) / |MA30_t|
percentile(x_t) = (# {v ≤ x_t}) / N over a defined reference set
Anchor: #mental-model
Moving averages (MA7 / MA30)
Basic
A moving average smooths daily noise by averaging recent days. MA7 is short-term smoothing; MA30 is the broader baseline. Comparing MA7 vs MA30 helps you see whether the short-term regime sits above or below the structural baseline.
Advanced
MA_n(t) = (1/n) · Σ_{i=0..n-1} x_{t-i}
Defined only when all n inputs are non-null; otherwise MA_n(t) = null.
We intentionally avoid “partial window” averages because they change the meaning of MA_n.
Anchor: #moving-averages
Percentile
Basic
Percentile tells you how unusual today is compared with other days in the selected window. Example: 90th percentile means today is higher than most days in the window.
Advanced
Given V = {x_i} (non-null) in the reference window:
percentile(x_t) = ( # { v ∈ V : v ≤ x_t } ) / |V|
Reported as 0..100. Null when |V| is too small.
Anchor: #percentile
Coverage & missing days
Basic
Coverage tells you whether the selected window has complete data. Missing days are not treated as zero. If coverage is low, interpretations should be treated as less robust.
Advanced
expected_days = # UTC dates in [start, end]
present_days = # rows present
missing_days = expected_days − present_days (with explicit date list)
nonNull_ratio = (# non-null daily values) / expected_days
Anchor: #coverage
Freshness / lag
Basic
Freshness tells you how up-to-date the dataset is (as-of date and lag). Different chains can legitimately have different lags.
Advanced
lag_days = (today_utc_date − asof_date)
Displayed as: as-of YYYY-MM-DD (lag Nd)
Anchor: #freshness
Z-score (standardized deviation)
Basic
Z-score expresses how far a value is from the mean in standard deviation units. It helps compare “unusualness” across metrics with different units.
Advanced
z_t = (x_t − μ) / σ
μ = mean(V), σ = stdev(V), V = non-null values in the reference window
If σ is ~0 or sample too small → z is null.
Anchor: #z-score
Practical usage

How to read the platform

Landing (30-second scan)
Basic
  1. MA7 vs MA30: short-term regime vs structural baseline.
  2. Daily vs MA7: one-day deviation vs short-term norm.
  3. Percentile: whether today is extreme or typical within the selected window.
  4. Click through for deeper context and audit signals.
Advanced
The landing page intentionally focuses on the four primitives and avoids raw links/coverage detail to keep the scan fast.
Dashboards expose data-quality and reproducibility links; wiki defines semantics; methodology defines global rules.
Dashboards (audit & depth)
Basic
Use dashboards when you want detail: coverage, lag, missing days, and additional metrics. These are still descriptive.
Advanced
Professionals can reproduce charts from the exported JSON artifacts (gold/derived/meta) using the documented rules.
1) Fetch reference series (e.g., last365d).
2) Compute MA/context stats on reference series.
3) Slice display window last.

Daily transactions

Key: tx_count_daily
See methodology: /methodology#tx_count_daily
#tx_count_daily
Basic
What it is
Counts how many transactions were recorded that day.
How it’s computed
Read as a single numeric value from the published daily gold file for each date.
Why it’s included
It is a direct, price-agnostic proxy for day-to-day network usage.
Value to the user
Helps you see whether activity is low/typical/elevated versus the chain’s own recent history.
Advanced
What it is
Daily transaction count for the chain (unit: transactions/day).
How it’s computed
Gold field: tx_count_daily from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. The UI contextualizes the raw series with MA7/MA30 (from derived where available, otherwise computed as a trailing average over available days).
Why it’s included
Transaction count is a core demand/activity proxy. Interpretation should rely on smoothed trends (MA7/MA30) and explicit coverage/freshness rather than single-day spikes.
Value to the user
Supports regime/context reading: sustained deviations from baseline are more informative than isolated peaks. Use alongside fees/utilization to distinguish demand from subsidized or low-cost activity.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Active addresses

Key: unique_active_addresses
See methodology: /methodology#unique_active_addresses
#unique_active_addresses
Basic
What it is
Counts how many unique addresses were active that day (sent or received a transaction).
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline and written as a daily gold numeric field.
Why it’s included
It approximates participation breadth rather than raw throughput.
Value to the user
Helps distinguish broad participation from activity driven by a small number of entities.
Advanced
What it is
Unique active addresses per day (unit: addresses/day), as defined by the pipeline’s address-activity logic.
How it’s computed
Gold field: unique_active_addresses from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Exact activity definition can vary by chain data model (e.g., UTXO vs account-based); see methodology caveats.
Why it’s included
Transaction count can rise due to batching or spam; unique actives helps contextualize whether activity is broad-based or concentrated.
Value to the user
Useful for regime/context reading: a rising tx_count_daily with flat unique_active_addresses can indicate concentration, batching, or repeated interactions by fewer entities.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Median transaction fee (native)

Key: median_tx_fee_native
See methodology: /methodology#median_tx_fee_native
#median_tx_fee_native
Basic
What it is
The median fee paid per transaction that day, denominated in the chain’s native token.
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline from per-transaction fee data, then summarized as a daily median.
Why it’s included
It describes fee pressure and competition for limited capacity without using price.
Value to the user
Shows whether typical transaction costs are low/typical/elevated versus recent history.
Advanced
What it is
Median per-transaction fee in native units (median across transactions observed on the date).
How it’s computed
Gold field: median_tx_fee_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Fee definition follows chain conventions (e.g., gas_used * effective_gas_price for EVM chains, fee components for BTC).
Why it’s included
A descriptive friction signal: higher typical fees often co-occur with congestion or higher willingness-to-pay for inclusion, but does not imply value judgment.
Value to the user
Helps contextualize activity: rising transactions with rising median fee suggests capacity pressure; rising transactions with flat/low fees suggests slack capacity or subsidized usage.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Gas utilization

Key: gas_utilization_pct
See methodology: /methodology#gas_utilization_pct
#gas_utilization_pct
Basic
What it is
How full blocks were on average that day, expressed as a percent of capacity.
How it’s computed
Computed from block-level utilization and aggregated to a daily average by the pipeline.
Why it’s included
It is a descriptive capacity-pressure signal.
Value to the user
Helps you understand whether the chain was capacity-constrained over the period.
Advanced
What it is
Daily average of gas_used / gas_limit (or equivalent capacity metric), expressed as percent.
How it’s computed
Gold field: gas_utilization_pct from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. For non-EVM chains this metric may be structurally not applicable and is expected to be null.
Why it’s included
Utilization helps interpret fee and activity trends: high utilization indicates blocks are near capacity; low utilization indicates slack.
Value to the user
Pairs with fee and transaction trends to distinguish demand spikes from capacity expansion or slack regimes. Useful for regime context without any price signal.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Failed transaction rate

Key: failed_tx_rate
See methodology: /methodology#failed_tx_rate
#failed_tx_rate
Basic
What it is
The share of transactions that failed that day (as a percent).
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline from transaction status outcomes, then aggregated daily.
Why it’s included
It describes execution friction and potential UX degradation without implying blame.
Value to the user
Helps you see whether execution was smooth or error-prone versus recent history.
Advanced
What it is
Daily failure ratio (failed / total) expressed as percent, based on chain-specific failure semantics.
How it’s computed
Gold field: failed_tx_rate from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. For chains where failure semantics are not available or not meaningful, the metric may be null.
Why it’s included
Failure rate helps interpret demand: high activity with elevated failures can indicate congestion, mispriced fees, or application-level issues.
Value to the user
Useful as an operational context signal: persistent increases can coincide with congestion regimes or ecosystem events (without implying causality).
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Average block time (seconds)

Key: avg_block_time_sec
See methodology: /methodology#avg_block_time_sec
#avg_block_time_sec
Basic
What it is
Average time between blocks that day (in seconds).
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline from consecutive block timestamps and averaged daily.
Why it’s included
It is an operational stability indicator.
Value to the user
Helps you see whether block production was stable versus recent history.
Advanced
What it is
Daily average block interval (seconds) based on observed block timestamps.
How it’s computed
Gold field: avg_block_time_sec from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Interpretation differs by chain (e.g., PoW variance vs fixed-slot systems).
Why it’s included
Block time captures production cadence. Persistent deviations can indicate operational or protocol-level conditions, without implying causality.
Value to the user
Useful for context: changing cadence affects throughput and user experience. Combine with block_count and activity for a fuller picture.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Blocks per day

Key: block_count_daily
See methodology: /methodology#block_count_daily
#block_count_daily
Basic
What it is
Counts how many blocks were produced that day.
How it’s computed
Read from the pipeline’s gold daily output as a single numeric value per date.
Why it’s included
It describes production output and operational regularity.
Value to the user
Helps you detect days/weeks with unusual production output.
Advanced
What it is
Daily block count (unit: blocks/day) from observed on-chain block production.
How it’s computed
Gold field: block_count_daily from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Closely related to avg_block_time_sec but more robust to outliers in time deltas.
Why it’s included
Block count is a stability/throughput context metric and is often easier to interpret than raw timestamp variance.
Value to the user
Useful for regime context: persistent deviations can co-occur with outages, reorganizations, or design changes, without implying causality.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Value transferred (native)

Key: value_transferred_native
See methodology: /methodology#value_transferred_native
#value_transferred_native
Basic
What it is
Total amount of the native token transferred on-chain that day.
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline as a daily aggregate of transfers and written to the gold file.
Why it’s included
It provides an economic-throughput proxy without using any price data.
Value to the user
Helps you see whether activity is associated with larger settlement flows or mostly small transfers.
Advanced
What it is
Daily sum of native token value transferred (native units/day), as computed by the pipeline.
How it’s computed
Gold field: value_transferred_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Transfer accounting is chain-specific (e.g., UTXO outputs vs account transfers); see caveats.
Why it’s included
Value transferred complements activity metrics: high activity can be spammy; value transferred can indicate economic weight, still price-agnostic.
Value to the user
Supports context reading: divergence between tx_count and value_transferred can indicate changes in typical transfer size or usage mix, without implying motives.
If any of these fields show “—”, the metric is missing a required documentation block in the catalog.

Median transaction value (native)

Key: median_tx_value_native
See methodology: /methodology#median_tx_value_native
#median_tx_value_native
Basic
What it is
Median value transferred per transaction that day, denominated in the chain’s native token.
How it’s computed
Computed by the pipeline from per-transaction transferred value and summarized as a daily median.
Why it’s included
It adds context to activity and total value transferred.
Value to the user
Helps you see whether typical transfers are small/typical/large versus recent history.
Advanced
What it is
Median per-transaction transferred value in native units (median across transactions observed on the date).
How it’s computed
Gold field: median_tx_value_native from public/data/published/v1/gold/<chain>/YYYY-MM-DD.json. Exact definition depends on how transfers are extracted per chain (UTXO vs account-based).
Why it’s included
Median transfer size helps interpret whether changes in total value are broad-based or dominated by a small number of large transfers.
Value to the user
Use with tx_count and value_transferred: rising total value with stable tx_count can indicate larger typical transfers; rising tx_count with falling median value can indicate smaller typical transfers.
